clue.text: E. Nesbit's lover found wanting

definitions.meaning: Nesbit's novel The ... Amorist names its lover by this adjective
lacking something, not whole or finished

explanation.surface: A novelist's sweetheart turns out to be a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesbit titled a novel The Incomplete Amorist, and anything found wanting is deficient or unfinished.

clue.text: "Most people have a furious to talk about themselves" (Maugham)

definitions.text: "Most people have a furious to talk about themselves" (Maugham)

parts.words: "Most people have a furious to talk about themselves" (Maugham)
parts.note: a Maugham quotation with one word missing after furious; the solver supplies the noun for a strong urge

explanation.surface: A quotation from Somerset Maugham on human vanity, with a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A furious urge or craving is what fills the gap in Maugham's line about self-absorption.

clue.text: A group of Auel's Earth's children

definitions.text: A group of Auel's Earth's children

parts.words: A group of Auel's Earth's children
parts.note: Jean Auel's Earth's Children series opens with The ... of the Cave Bear; a family group is the general sense

explanation.surface: A band of characters from Jean Auel's prehistoric novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal kin group, and the Neanderthal tribe in Auel's The Clan of the Cave Bear.

clue.text: "Select words so ingeniously misapplied"

parts.note: Captain Absolute's description of Mrs Malaprop's speech in Sheridan's The Rivals

explanation.surface: A quotation praising cleverly misused vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd word substitutions, named after Sheridan's Mrs Malaprop, are exactly words misapplied.

clue.text: Some stately pieces in otherwise silent interlude

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the words silent interlude, a run otherwise belonging to those words

explanation.surface: Grand musical movements played within a quiet break.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'silent interlude'. Lento is the musical marking for slow, stately playing; its Italian plural is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow movements marked lento in music; the Italian plural names several such stately pieces.

clue.text: Reluctant choice of husband by Laetitia Dale

definitions.text: Reluctant choice of husband by Laetitia Dale

parts.words: Reluctant choice of husband by Laetitia Dale
parts.note: in Meredith's novel Laetitia Dale finally and unwillingly accepts Sir Willoughby Patterne, the title figure

explanation.surface: A heroine grudgingly accepts a suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Meredith's novel is named for Sir Willoughby, the self-centred man Laetitia Dale reluctantly marries.

clue.text: Apply the acid test to art?

definitions.text: Apply the acid test to art?

parts.words: Apply the acid test to art?
parts.note: printmakers bite a metal plate with acid to make a picture, so acid is literally applied in art

explanation.surface: Putting artworks under the strictest scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving a plate by corroding it with acid is how an artist makes this kind of print.

clue.text: Result of Italian scorched earth policy?

definitions.text: Result of Italian scorched earth policy?

parts.words: Result of Italian scorched earth policy?
parts.note: the Italian words mean baked earth, so scorching earth yields this fired clay

explanation.surface: The aftermath of a military retreat in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fired clay pottery whose Italian name literally means cooked earth.

clue.text: Each put the strange ancient history books in first place

definitions.text: ancient history books in first place

indicators.note: something strange is odd or out of order, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone oddly puts old history volumes at the front of the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the letters of EACH PUT THE. The definition means the first seven books of the Old Testament, which stand first in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening seven books of the Bible, ancient scripture placed first in the canon.

clue.text: Conan Doyle's maverick zoologist calls out

definitions.meaning: Professor George Edward ... leads the expedition in The Lost World
here read as one who calls out, that is someone who dares or disputes; the definition is a verb phrase standing for an agent noun

explanation.surface: A fictional scientist summons people loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doyle's Professor of The Lost World, and a person who issues a dare or contests a title.

clue.text: Sheridan had a sort of relapse taking one to Scarborough

definitions.text: Sheridan had a sort of relapse taking one to Scarborough

parts.words: Sheridan had a sort of relapse taking one to Scarborough
parts.note: Sheridan's play A ... to Scarborough reworks Vanbrugh's The Relapse; a stumble is a sort of relapse

explanation.surface: A playwright falls ill again on a seaside journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarborough is a seaside resort in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble or a journey: both senses meet in the title of Sheridan's adaptation of The Relapse.

clue.text: Somerset rose fancier

parts.note: in Henry VI Part 1 the Earl of Somerset plucks the red rose in the Temple Garden, so he fancies that rose

explanation.surface: A gardener from the English county of Somerset who loves roses.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset reads as the English county, but it is a title: John Beaufort, Earl (later Duke) of Somerset, who chose the Lancastrian red rose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beaufort nobleman holding the Somerset title, who picks the red rose of Lancaster in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Beethoven's seasonal music used by parson, at all events

parts.note: a season, the one after winter

indicators.note: the letters are borrowed from inside the words that follow, used by them as part of their spelling

explanation.surface: A clergyman plays Beethoven's season-themed piece on every occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' marks the run SONATA hidden in 'parSON AT All'. The definition is loose: Beethoven's work, with 'music' and 'events' padding the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Violin Sonata No 5 in F is nicknamed for the season of new growth.

clue.text: Issuer of final notices

parts.note: reads like a debt collector, but the last notices anyone gets are death notices in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A clerk sending last-warning bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who writes accounts of the newly dead, the last write-up of a life.

clue.text: Contents of commonplace book?

parts.note: a commonplace book collects quotations, but a book of commonplaces would hold trite remarks

explanation.surface: What fills a scrapbook of quotations.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite, overused remarks are commonplaces, so a book of them would be full of these.

clue.text: Tolstoy loosely links books to tragic prince

indicators.note: held loosely, the letters of the two words fall out of order and are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder words, with one S too many as printed

explanation.surface: Tolstoy casually ties volumes to a doomed royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges LINKS BOOK(S). Prince Andrei is the tragic hero of Tolstoy's War and Peace; the printed fodder has an extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrei of that family dies of wounds after Borodino in War and Peace.

clue.text: Banks' activity in respect of those coming through

definitions.text: Banks' activity in respect of those coming through

parts.words: Banks' activity in respect of those coming through
parts.note: suggests a bank's dealings, but customs officers at a border check the travellers passing through

explanation.surface: How banks handle incoming payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs officers frisk and inspect travellers, a thorough probing look at each person.

clue.text: Garcia Marquez said he writes to an officer

definitions.text: Garcia Marquez said he writes to an officer

parts.words: Garcia Marquez said he writes to an officer
parts.note: the title's subject is the person who does the writing

explanation.surface: A Colombian novelist claims he corresponds with a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody: Garcia Marquez's title says nobody writes to the colonel, a military officer.

clue.text: Sign of musical togetherness

parts.note: a direction in a score telling every performer to play at once

explanation.surface: Evidence that a band plays well together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian marking for all players together, as opposed to a solo passage.

clue.text: Such an account of Shakespeare's mss came from Ireland

definitions.text: Such an account of Shakespeare's mss came from Ireland

parts.words: Such an account of Shakespeare's mss came from Ireland
parts.note: William Henry Ireland forged Shakespeare manuscripts and swore they were genuine

explanation.surface: A report on Shakespeare's manuscripts arrived from the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ireland reads as the country but is the forger William Henry Ireland, who passed off his own manuscripts as Shakespeare's in the 1790s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland vouched for his forged papers as genuine, the very opposite of what they were.

clue.text: Smith's first success strangely occurs after a fall

indicators.note: the rearranged word follows the season in the answer

parts.note: fall is the American word for the season

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of the next word appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's breakthrough comes oddly right after a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodie Smith, later author of The Hundred and One Dalmatians, first succeeded with this 1931 play. 'fall' is the American name for the season; 'strangely' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodie Smith's breakthrough play of 1931, named after the flower that blooms late in the year.

clue.text: Final letter from Aristophanes, perhaps

parts.note: Aristophanes is an example of a Greek, and the last letter of the Greek alphabet is meant, not a last message

explanation.surface: The playwright's last piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing character of the Greek alphabet, the one any Greek such as Aristophanes would end on.

clue.text: Nothing in noise produced by Beaumont and Fletcher's father of cross-dressing daughter

definitions.text: Beaumont and Fletcher's father of cross-dressing daughter

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the word for noise

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Jacobean play's racket introduces a father whose daughter dresses as a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Beaumont and Fletcher's Philaster, the lord Dion's daughter Euphrasia disguises herself as the page Bellario.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtier in Philaster whose daughter serves the hero disguised as a boy page.

clue.text: Deity's dual existence at Oxford

indicators.note: dual means twofold, so the word for existing is written twice

parts.note: is expresses existence, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: A god leads a double life at the university town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deity's' gives the definition plus 's for 'is'. 'at Oxford' adds a further hint: the Thames is called the Isis as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mother goddess, also the name of the Thames at Oxford.

clue.text: Film not made by major production company — but still in the race

definitions.text: Film not made by major production company
definitions.meaning: an independent film, made outside the big studios
the ... 500 and IndyCar series are motor races, so a driver still competing is in that race

explanation.surface: An independent film that is still in contention for awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for independent cinema, and the Indianapolis motor race.

clue.text: Eve's libido re-examined by Waugh

indicators.note: looked at again in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Evelyn Waugh takes a fresh look at the first woman's sex drive.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is the hyphenated word after 'libido'. The answer is Evelyn Waugh's 1930 novel of Bright Young Things, so 'by Waugh' defines it as one of his works.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's second novel, a satire on 1920s London society.

clue.text: Murderess who married an angel . .

parts.note: Hardy's heroine weds Angel Clare and later kills Alec d'Urberville

explanation.surface: A killer who wed a heavenly being.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's heroine of the d'Urbervilles, who marries Angel Clare and stabs Alec.

clue.text: … angel Stein wrongly identified with wild roses

indicators.note: wrongly identified suggests letters put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gertrude Stein is mistakenly taken for an angel among wild roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges ANGEL STEIN. The definition is the sweetbriar, a wild rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbriars, a kind of wild rose with fragrant leaves.
